b_records.quote: Let Xi ~ GZD(thetai), i = 1, 2 be two random variables. If theta1 >= theta2, then X1 ≺lr X2, X1 ≺hr X2, X1 ≺s X2 and X1 <=cx X2. Proof. We have fX1(t)/fX2(t) = (sum_{k=0}^n ak k!/theta2^{k+1})/(sum_{k=0}^n ak k!/theta1^{k+1}) * e^{-(theta1 - theta2) t}. For simplification, we use ln(fX1(t)/fX2(t)). Now, we can find d/dt ln(fX1(t)/fX2(t)) = -(theta1 - theta2). To this end, if theta1 >= theta2, we have d/dt ln(fX1(t)/fX2(t)) <= 0. This means that X1 ≺lr X2. Also, according to Remark 3 the theorem is proved.
